justification: One-click 'Start my plan' commits to $29.99 charge with no confirmation step: s1 shows 'Charged — no confirmation language' (no 'Are you sure?'/'Confirm purchase'), only promotional copy around the button.
8-policy comparison table makes the actual differences (excess, breakdown cover, courtesy car) explicit side-by-side; clear header tells user what separates the policies; no manipulation.

The $5.00/month fee and auto-renewal exist only inside a collapsed <details> and a hover tooltip on the CTA; the visible button reads 'Start 7-day free trial' with no fee shown — fee concealed until after the user commits.

Dense manufactured urgency: 'LIMITED TIME', 'only 3 left', 'selling fast', 'flash deal', 'ends soon', 'Last chance', 'don't miss out', 'one-time' — 8 urgency tokens in 27 words (density 29.6/100), plus 'Only 3 left' badge; pressure copy to force the purchase.
Donation prompt offers 'Yes, add a $2 donation' vs neutral 'No, thanks' — declining carries no emotional tax (sentiment roughly equal); both options emotionally affordable, no shaming.

Default consent text is deliberately obfuscatory legalese ('proprietary algorithmic methodologies... commercialization of your personal information to third-party data brokers') that hides what is actually being agreed to; plain-English translation is hidden behind a button, so the visible default is an uninformed-consent maze.

Decline option forces the user to assert 'No, I don't care about the environment' (sentiment -0.81) vs accept 'Yes, I care about the planet' (+0.72) — semantic asymmetry manufactures guilt to steer toward the $2 donation.

Offer copy is persuasive but shares identical typography/weight/area with the factual copy (weight ratio 1.0); 'Not now' is a real equal option; offer stands on its own merits — emphasis does not do the persuading.
Subscription management is calm and factual: all four options (keep/pause/downgrade/cancel) equally styled, cancel takes effect at end of period, no threats or countdowns — genuinely user-respecting.

Renewal countdown runs at 1.5s (below ~2.0s reaction baseline) and the DOM contains no cancel affordance at all ('No cancel button' badge; 'cancel not in the dom'); the only options are to let it renew or proceed — user is automated into payment.

A pulsing countdown banner (02:59:41) dominates ~75% of the panel in high-saturation red-orange with 'last chance'/'Ending soon' labels; the artificial deadline is turned into the central visual event to pressure the user into claiming the reward.

Battle mode pits the user against another person ('Beat Alex to win the crown! The loser gets demoted a league') with a live score gap (0 vs 70) — competitive shaming designed to provoke engagement at the expense of the opponent.
Storage notice is factual and dismissible: 'This notice can be dismissed; your data is not at risk', calm explanation, upgrade optional after a deliberate choice — no entrapment, no pressure.
Invite-friends mechanic is a single muted line under the real content (area ratio 0.08 < 0.3), explicitly labeled optional; recruitment stays secondary to the app's core utility.
Accept All and Reject All are rendered with equal bounding boxes, contrast and z-index (P ratio 1.0); text states both options carry the same visual weight — the eye is not steered toward consent.

Recruitment banner consumes 0.55 of the viewport (progress bar, tier badges, live counter, dual CTAs, 'Only 2 friends away from exclusive rewards!') while the actual app content is squeezed below — gamified invite pyramid elevated to a core interface function.

Visual weight ratio ~10.2 (vs threshold 4): 'Accept all cookies' is a large filled rose button while 'Reject all' is an 8px pale gray text link — rejection path is relationally suppressed; 43 partners set tracking cookies.

'Accept All' is the only element styled as a button (large filled block, probability 0.86) vs tiny gray 'Manage options' link (0.06); ratio 14.3 >> 2.0 — gaze is structurally steered into consent; no direct reject control.
